condition: Pre-operative assessment (ASA I, elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy)
summary: 32-year-old fit woman (ASA I, good functional capacity, not pregnant) listed for day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative assessment for planned gallbladder operation
inputs.hpi: Three episodes of right upper quadrant colic over 8 months, each settling within 4 hours. Ultrasound showed gallstones. Listed for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Well between attacks. Climbs three flights of stairs without stopping. Last menstrual period 9 days ago.

exam.general: Well. HR 72, BP 118/74, RR 14, SpO2 99% on air, T 36.7°C. BMI 24.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple mobile gallstones, gallbladder wall 2 mm, no pericholecystic fluid. CBD 4 mm. Liver normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Pre-operative assessment — symptomatic gallstones for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic cholelithiasis. Fit for day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy. ASA I.

emergencyLevel.note: Elective pre-operative assessment of a well patient: not an emergency or same-day problem.

recommended.note: ASA grade is recorded for every anaesthetic. Web CDS pre-op triggers read procedureData.preop (Perioperative tab), which the harness does not set; the ASA rule also fires on pre-op symptom words or comorbidities.
recommended.knownGapNote: getCdsSuggestions suggests only asge-cbd and news2. The ASA rule fires on pre-op symptom words or comorbidities, none present in a fit patient; the procedureData.preop trigger (Perioperative tab) is not set by the harness, so this may pass in the app once that tab is filled.
recommended.proposedFix: Trigger ASA on encounter type (pre-operative assessment / elective surgery visit) and on a confirmed operative plan, not only on symptom words.

mustExclude.note: NICE NG45: do not routinely offer haemostasis tests before elective surgery (ASA 1, intermediate surgery).
NICE NG45: no ECG for ASA 1 intermediate surgery without cardiovascular disease.

mustInclude.note: NICE NG45: on the day of surgery ask women of childbearing potential whether they could be pregnant and offer a test with consent.

mustExclude.note: ESA 2011: clear fluids up to 2 h, solids up to 6 h; "nil by mouth from midnight" prolongs fasting.
SIGN 104: antibiotic prophylaxis is not recommended for low-risk laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: NICE NG45 — Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
guideline.section: Tables by surgical grade and ASA grade: ASA 1 minor/intermediate surgery — no routine FBC, U&E, ECG or haemostasis tests; do not routinely offer haemostasis tests (consider only for ASA 3–4 with chronic liver disease or when anticoagulant management needs it); ask women of childbearing potential about possible pregnancy and offer a test with consent
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery (NG45). London: NICE; 2016.

guideline.name: ASA Physical Status Classification System
guideline.section: ASA I healthy; ASA II mild systemic disease; ASA III severe systemic disease; ASA IV severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life; E suffix for emergency surgery
guideline.citation: American Society of Anesthesiologists. ASA Physical Status Classification System (last amended 13 December 2020).

guideline.name: ESA guideline — perioperative fasting in adults and children
guideline.section: Clear fluids up to 2 h and solids up to 6 h before elective anaesthesia; prolonged fasting should be avoided
guideline.citation: Smith I, Kranke P, Murat I, et al. Perioperative fasting in adults and children: guidelines from the European Society of Anaesthesiology. Eur J Anaesthesiol. 2011;28:556–69.

guideline.name: SIGN 104 — Antibiotic prophylaxis in surgery
guideline.section: Procedure table: laparoscopic cholecystectomy — prophylaxis not recommended in low-risk patients (consider in high risk); open inguinal/femoral hernia repair with mesh — recommended/consider; colorectal surgery — highly recommended; a single dose is sufficient for most procedures; no evidence for post-operative doses
guideline.citation: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. Antibiotic prophylaxis in surgery (SIGN 104). Edinburgh: SIGN; 2008, updated 2014.

rationale: Base pre-operative case: a fit young adult for intermediate (laparoscopic) surgery. Tests the ASA prompt, NICE NG45 test minimisation (no routine clotting or ECG), pregnancy status, fasting advice and routine prophylactic antibiotics. Every other pre-operative vignette permutes this one.
